source.title: Harm-Conditioned Computational Friction as a Contrastive Diagnostic of Safety Representations in Language Models: A Proof-of-Concept and Control Audit

page_placements.theme: Direction estimation: sensitivity to prompt sets, baselines, labels, layer, normalisation and outlier channels, and estimator reliability

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper builds a diagnostic around an H–N difference-in-means direction and directional ablation, but reports perturbation measures rather than refusal or compliance behavior. It therefore uses the finding as a tool without testing the refusal claim.
record.gate_note: The paper applies centered positive-only ablation and reports KL divergence, final-logit L2 distance, and projection contrasts. It does not report refusal/compliance outcomes, add the direction, edit model weights, or test capability preservation, so these measurements cannot establish the behavioral effects named in the claim versions. The cited original study's results are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study builds an H–N difference-in-means direction and applies centered positive-only ablation on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct. It reports only perturbation metrics (KL divergence, logit L2, projection contrasts), with no refusal or compliance rates, no direction addition, no weight edit and no capability checks. It uses the refusal-direction method as a tool for its own diagnostic and does not test whether the direction mediates refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that HCCF detects a label-conditioned, domain-general unsafe/refusable-request representation and works as an internal audit protocol. They say it is not a validated alignment-robustness measure or a causal safety guarantee.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a build-set H–N mean-difference direction and ablation, but centers projection on the neutral mean, removes only positive displacement, targets the final prompt-token representation at a selected normalization layer, and measures perturbation rather than refusal behavior. No direction addition is tested.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported perturbation contrasts change with prompt construction and label condition: placeholder wording produces larger signals, format-only inputs attenuate them, label-shuffling preserves most of the balanced signal, and label derangement or polarity reversal inverts the semantic contrast.

fits_no_version.finding: On the balanced benchmark, centered positive-only ablation perturbs H prompts more than N or B prompts (KL H–N 0.2488, B–N 0.0483, H–B 0.2005). Borderline prompts are also displaced.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An H–N mean-difference direction yields an H-specific internal perturbation contrast in a small instruct model, but it is not a clean harmfulness-only boundary.

fits_no_version.finding: Placeholder wording inflated the contrasts (KL 0.6334 vs 0.2488), and the artifact-control placeholder run kept most of that inflated signal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-wording artifacts can inflate H–N direction ablation contrasts.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the controls: the H=N null collapsed, the format-only null attenuated, label-shuffle preserved most of the effect, and derangement and polarity swap inverted the semantic contrast.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The contrastive direction is domain-general and follows the assigned labels rather than independently detecting semantic harmfulness.

record.problems: The experiment uses 10 matched triples, with 5 for direction construction and 5 for held-out evaluation, and tests only one model. Prompts are abstract and non-operational. No confidence intervals, paired tests, or capability-preservation checks are reported, and the paper does not pair perturbation measures with behavioral refusal outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: None. The reported perturbation contrasts and control conditions are included. No behavioral refusal or compliance results are reported.

untested.parts: No refusal/compliance outcome after ablation, no direction addition, no capability preservation measure.
No weight edit or released-model refusal evaluation.
No jailbreak evaluation or adversarial training.
Single-direction assumption is stated as a limitation (Sec 9.4); no alternative tested.
The authors name separating harm intent from refusal as future work (Sec 10); no measurement of it.
No cross-language, variant or base-to-instruct transfer.

record.verdict_notes: Preprint. One 0.5B model, 5 build and 5 held-out triples, no uncertainty reported. The original study is cited as ref [10] only as motivation. All rows correctly carry versions ['none'] with state cannot_determine, because the perturbation metrics cannot show refusal removal or induction.

versions.untested_parts: No refusal or compliance outcome, direction addition, or general-capability measure.
No weight edit or released-model refusal evaluation.
No jailbreak or attack evaluation, and no training against ablation.
The paper notes that representations may be multidimensional or nonlinear, but does not test alternatives to one direction.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.

relation.reason: Cites [10] (Arditi et al.) and reuses its direction construction and ablation. Its results bear on its own audit protocol, not on whether the direction mediates refusal.

tranche.reason: Builds an Arditi-style H–N difference-in-means direction as a tool and reports only its own diagnostic's perturbation metrics (KL, logit L2, projection). It reports no refusal or compliance rates, no addition, no weight edit and no capability check.

source_check.notes: Tiny proof of concept: one model (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), 5 build and 5 held-out abstract triples, no CIs, no refusal outcomes. The polarity swap stays positive under assigned labels (+0.2574) and inverts only under semantic labels (-0.2574). Table 1's layout is scrambled in the text, but every value checked here is confirmed in Sections 7.1 to 7.5.

statements.problem: none; 0.6334 (public placeholder run) and 0.2488 (balanced abstract benchmark) are both held-out final-token KL H–N contrasts on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (Table 1). The inversions it describes are under the original semantic labels.
